reply_text:
Musk's 2016 record holds two new dated self-driving forecasts. I found both only in news reports, not in his own words, and found nothing dated about AGI or AI in general.

- **June 1, Code Conference:** Bloomberg's report, reprinted by IndustryWeek, quotes him saying full self-driving is less than two years off, with regulators taking at least another year.
- **October 19, Autopilot hardware press call:** CNBC quotes him saying the goal is a fully self-driving demonstration from LA to New York by the end of 2017.
- **January 10, press call:** Malay Mail (Reuters) quotes his two-year forecast for summoning a car from LA to New York. That looks like the claim already in your summon-anywhere file. The same report says, in its own words rather than his, that he thought fully self-driving cars would be technically possible within 24 to 36 months. I left that out because there is no direct quote.

Things to know before checking:
- **Code Conference transcript:** The fan transcript I opened (shitelonsays.com) is unfinished and stops before the self-driving section, so I couldn't check the June quote against his own words.
- **AI risk at the same talk:** Coverage of his "neural lace" and "house cats" remarks gave no date or time span, so nothing qualified.
- **October call transcript:** One site with a transcript of the call (xautoworld.com) wouldn't open; it showed a "verifying your request" page instead.
- **Master Plan, Part Deux (July 20):** I read a copy on a Tesla owners' club site, not tesla.com. It puts a mileage figure on regulatory approval but gives no date, so it isn't listed.
- **Budget:** I used all 6 page openings and 10 of the 12 searches. One search was wasted: its results were lost to a coding error before I could read them, so it ran once with nothing found.
